subject: Re: AvaTech + Redwood — integration scoping, SDK/auth, and prompt governance playbook
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Erin Patel <erin@avatech.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: AvaTech call recap + next steps (SDK/auth, routing, prompts)

Hi Erin — great to speak earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Call highlights:
- Primary use case: in-product help and multi-document summarization for customer support agents (latency target: 200–400ms p50 on short prompts, batch reranks overnight).
- Data residency: US-only; may expand to EU next year.
- Security: SOC2 in scope; security team will want API auth details and audit log samples.

Open technical questions we flagged on the call (would love confirmations from your eng/security):
1) Auth model: do you prefer API key scoped to a service account, or mutual-TLS / workload identity for server-to-server calls?
2) Routing & fallbacks: will you want single-region routing (us-west) or active-active across us-west/us-east with automatic fallback?
3) Embeddings & reranking: which index volume do you expect (approx #docs)? Will you want host-side embeddings or Redwood-managed embeddings endpoints?
4) Structured output & tool-calling: do you need JSON-schema enforced outputs (we can instrument tool-calls + consistency checks) vs free-text?
5) Prompt governance: do you have an existing prompt versioning system / red-team process, or should we propose a lightweight starting playbook?

Immediate next steps we propose:
- Marcus to share a short SDK snippet (node/python) showing auth + structured output example. (ETA: 24h)
- AvaTech to send the network diagram and security contact (we noted security@avatech.ai).
- Schedule an engineering scoping session (30–45m) to map routing, embedding strategy, and rollout plan.

Attachments: draft SDK quickstart + list of common structured output examples.

If that matches your notes, I’ll schedule the scoping call and loop in our security lead.

Thanks again,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

Subject: Re: AvaTech call recap + next steps (SDK/auth, routing, prompts)

Thanks Hannah — thanks everyone for the time. Quick answers inline and attached a network diagram.

Inline answers:
1) Auth: we prefer scoped API keys for now tied to a per-service account. We are evaluating mTLS but that will be Q4 work.
2) Routing: start single-region (us-west) for rollout, with a plan to expand to us-east for redundancy. Automatic fallback sounds useful if you handle model-variant fallback.
3) Embeddings: initial index ~150k docs; we prefer Redwood-managed embeddings to avoid a separate infra burden, but need to understand retention and re-embedding cadence.
4) Structured output: we require strict JSON output for the agent actions (schema enforcement + validation). Tool-calling for internal ticket creation is required.
5) Prompt governance: we do not have a formal process — we’d appreciate a suggested playbook and a red-team exercise scope.

Attached: avatech-network-diagram.pdf
Security contact: security@avatech.ai (you can loop them into the next call).

Tom — I’ve added you for visibility on routing and infra.

Best,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: SDK snippets + architecture notes (structured output + rerank)

Hi Erin — following up with the SDK and a couple of runnable snippets that map to the items you flagged. I’m including small code excerpts below and attaching the quickstart PDF for the full examples.

Node (example: scoped API key auth + structured output enforcement):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west' });

const resp = await client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-1.3-instruct',
  input: prompt,
  output_schema: { type: 'object', properties: { action: { type: 'string' }, ticket_id: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['action'] },
  tool_calls: ['create_ticket'],
  stream: false
});

// resp.output validated against schema server-side; tool_calls trigger our tool-calling bridge to your ticketing endpoint

Routing and fallbacks:
- Default: single-region us-west pin for low-latency.
- Fallback policy: if p95 latency > 800ms or error-rate spike, route to us-east variant + model-compact fallback (still enforces schema).

Embeddings/Indexing approach:
- Redwood-managed embeddings: we recommend batch re-embed nightly for active docs and incremental for deltas.
- For 150k docs: recommend a hybrid index with approximate nearest neighbors + periodic dense re-embedding to keep freshness.

Prompt governance playbook (lightweight starter):
1) Prompt versioning: store canonical prompts in a repo (MD file or central config store) with semver (v0.1, v0.2). Every change requires a short PR describing intent, test prompts, and acceptance criteria.
2) Injection mitigations: enforce input sanitization on user fields, use role-based system prompts (system vs assistant vs user), and run a weekly prompt-injection fuzzer against high-traffic endpoints.
3) Red-team cadence: quarterly targeted red-team runs (top 5 intents), plus an annual company-wide exercise. Record regressions and tie to canary rollouts.
4) Monitoring & alerts: prompt-quality checks (answer drift, hallucination rates) and a dashboard for prompt changes vs eval failures.

Next steps I propose:
- Engineering scoping call (30–45m) to validate auth and ticketing integration — propose Wed May 13 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET.
- I’ll share a short mutual action plan doc and a sample security answers sheet for SOC2 artifacts.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf, security-answers-avatech.xlsx

Let me know if that time works.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
